# Jellyfin

Jellyfin is one of the two media servers; Plex is the other. Mediaplane runs the
upstream LinuxServer.io image, unmodified, when `media_server` is `jellyfin`.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by "pnpm docs:generate" from app.ts. Do not edit. -->

## What Mediaplane sets

- **Image:** `lscr.io/linuxserver/jellyfin:12.2ubu2604-ls53`
- **Digest:** `sha256:1bb4f88d822a0510bb3604b68aacb80d77c1d2a30181e500090c65111b98723b`
- **Architectures:** amd64, arm64
- **Ports:** 8096/tcp (web), published as `network.bind` says; `apps.jellyfin.port` moves the host port
- **Volumes:** `<home>/appdata/jellyfin` → `/config`; the data folder (`paths.data`) → `/data`
- **Runs as:** the stack's `user:`, through `PUID` and `PGID`
- **Health check:** `curl -fsS http://localhost:8096/health | grep -qx Healthy`, every 30s (timeout 10s, 5 retries, 120s to start)
- **Secrets:** `apiKey`: created by the app during its first-run setup
- **API:** on its `web` port, which Mediaplane reaches over the stack's wiring network, with `apiKey` in Jellyfin's `Authorization: MediaBrowser` header
- **Managed in the app:** `jellyfin.admin`: fields `jellyfin.admin.username`; the secret `password`, checked and never shown. `jellyfin.library_movies`: fields `jellyfin.library_movies.name` (fixed), `jellyfin.library_movies.collectionType` (fixed), `jellyfin.library_movies.paths`. `jellyfin.library_shows`: fields `jellyfin.library_shows.name` (fixed), `jellyfin.library_shows.collectionType` (fixed), `jellyfin.library_shows.paths`
- **Needs:** nothing
- **Provides:** `media-server`
- **Also turns on:** nothing

<!-- END GENERATED -->

## What Mediaplane does today

- **It runs Jellyfin** whenever `media_server` is `jellyfin`, listed under `apps` or not,
  with your data folder at `/data`.
- **It sets Jellyfin up before its web UI is published on your network.** Jellyfin's
  startup wizard answers whoever reaches it first, and whoever finishes it owns the
  server. So on its first start, Jellyfin has no published port. `apply` finishes the
  wizard over the stack's private wiring network, as the shared admin
  (`mediaplane credentials` shows the login), signs in, makes an API key named
  `Mediaplane`, keeps it in `state/secrets.json` at once, and signs out. Only then does
  it start Jellyfin again, with its web UI published as `network.bind` says.

  ```text
  up: Jellyfin, no port
    │
    ▼
  over the wiring network:
  the wizard, as the shared
  admin; sign in; the key,
  kept at once; sign out
    │
    ▼
  up again: Jellyfin
  published
  ```

  `plan` lists it under `First-run setup:`, and never runs it. A Jellyfin whose wizard is
  done, as its `system.xml` says, is never unpublished again. Before `apply` publishes
  Jellyfin, it asks once more whether its wizard is still open, and publishes it only if
  it is not: if it still looks open, `apply` stops and does not publish it. If the
  wizard was open when `apply` started Jellyfin, and the shared admin's sign-in is then
  refused, someone else finished it meanwhile: `apply` stops, and Jellyfin stays
  unpublished. Its wizard is now done, so the next `apply` would publish it: if you did
  not finish it yourself, start Jellyfin afresh first, as the
  [wiring failed runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md) says. If Mediaplane
  can't read `system.xml`, the error says so instead, since that may be a Jellyfin you
  set up yourself: fix the file, and don't start it afresh. With Jellyfin's key stored,
  `plan` warns (`bootstrap.unreadable`) that it can't tell whether the wizard is open:
  fix the ownership of `appdata/jellyfin`, or the user Mediaplane runs as.

- **The shared admin** (`jellyfin.admin`) is the user the wizard made, named as
  `admin.username`. A change of `admin.username` or `admin.password` reaches it through
  Jellyfin's API. `plan` and `apply` check its password by signing in and out again,
  which Jellyfin's activity log records, as it records any sign-in. Jellyfin doesn't
  lock its admin out after failed sign-ins.
- **Two libraries:** `Movies` (`jellyfin.library_movies`), of films, in
  `/data/media/movies`, and `Shows` (`jellyfin.library_shows`), of shows, in
  `/data/media/tv`: the folders Radarr and Sonarr file into. `apply` makes each folder
  first, as the stack's `user:`, in a throwaway Jellyfin container. A new library gets
  the options Jellyfin's own web UI gives one: the metadata and image downloaders that
  Jellyfin turns on by default, and new files picked up as they come. Its other settings
  are yours.
- **Sonarr and Radarr tell it of imports.** With them in the stack, each gets a
  connection to Jellyfin, `Jellyfin (Mediaplane)`, which has Jellyfin update its library
  when a file is imported, upgraded, renamed or deleted (see
  [Sonarr's](../sonarr/README.md) and [Radarr's](../radarr/README.md) READMEs).
- **Seerr signs in through it.** With Seerr in the stack, once Jellyfin is set up,
  `apply` signs Seerr in through Jellyfin as the shared admin, before Seerr is published
  (when `apply` runs the stack: see
  [T16](../../docs/security/threat-model.md#t16-someone-else-finishes-an-apps-first-run-setup)),
  and links Seerr to it with both libraries enabled (see
  [Seerr's README](../seerr/README.md)). That sign-in leaves Jellyfin a key named
  `Seerr`, and a device of Seerr's, which Seerr uses: leave them. Seerr's sign-in page
  then checks the shared admin login against Jellyfin.
- **A health check that waits for the server.** In the first seconds of every start,
  Jellyfin's `/health` answers `Degraded` while the server itself answers 503 to
  everything else, so the check passes only on `Healthy`. Its start period is 120
  seconds: failed checks don't count then, and the first that passes marks Jellyfin
  healthy.
- **Listing Plex as well** is an error, unless Plex says `enabled: false`.

## Drift and Keep mine

- **What drift reports.** `mediaplane drift`, and `plan`, report a change made in
  Jellyfin's web UI to what Mediaplane manages here, listed above under "Managed in the
  app": what Mediaplane set, and what Jellyfin holds now. A secret is checked with
  Jellyfin's own test, and named, never shown. `apply` puts each back.
- **Keeping yours.** `mediaplane keep jellyfin.<resource>.<field>`, as drift names it,
  keeps what Jellyfin holds instead: it adds the line under `overrides:` in `stack.yaml`,
  and `apply` then leaves it. A field marked `(fixed)` above, and a secret, can't be
  kept. `mediaplane keep jellyfin.library_movies` stops Mediaplane managing a resource deleted
  in Jellyfin. The [drift runbook](../../docs/runbooks/drift-reported.md) says more.
- **A folder added to `Movies` or `Shows`,** kept (`jellyfin.library_movies.paths`):
  the library then holds each folder kept, one comma-separated list. A folder with a
  comma in its name can't be listed: drift says so, and `apply` takes it out.
- **A library renamed in Jellyfin** is no longer found by its name: drift reports it
  deleted, and `apply` refuses to make it again while the renamed one holds its folder,
  saying what to do. Rename it back, or keep it as yours with
  `mediaplane keep jellyfin.library_movies` (or `library_shows`). Seerr then no longer
  enables it either.
- **Its admin password** is checked by drift once a day at most, while it passes: each
  check signs in, which Jellyfin's activity log keeps. `plan` and `apply` check it every
  time.

## Changing it

- **In `stack.yaml`,** under `apps.jellyfin`, you can set `port`, `version`, `env` and
  `hardware_transcoding`.
  The media server that `media_server` names can't be turned off with `enabled: false`:
  change `media_server` instead. A different `version` is an untested combination, and
  `plan` warns about it. See the
  [`stack.yaml` reference](../../docs/reference/stack-yaml.md).
- **The `Movies` and `Shows` libraries' names, what they hold and their folders** are
  Mediaplane's. A folder you add to one, or one of them you remove, is put back by the
  next `apply`, unless you keep it (see above). Add a library of your own instead.
  Everything else in them, such as their metadata language, is yours.
- **Hardware transcoding** (Intel Quick Sync, or AMD): set
  `hardware_transcoding: true` under `apps.jellyfin`. Mediaplane then gives Jellyfin the
  host's GPU (all of `/dev/dri`: the render node and the display node, as the image's own
  guide does), and `plan` checks the host has one. What it can't do for
  you:
  - load the GPU's driver on the host: `ls /dev/dri` should list `renderD128`. Recent
    Intel chips (12th gen, Arc) may need a recent kernel;
  - turn it on in Jellyfin: Dashboard, Playback, Transcoding, then Intel QuickSync
    (QSV) or VAAPI;
  - NVIDIA GPUs, which need Docker's NVIDIA runtime rather than `/dev/dri`. Add that in
    `compose.override.yaml` yourself.

  The pinned image's start-up gives Jellyfin's user the GPU's group (its
  `init-device-perms` step, checked on the pinned image), so no permissions need
  changing. CI has no GPU, so this is tested only as far as the Compose file and
  `plan`'s check; whether a stream really transcodes on the GPU shows in Jellyfin
  while you play something that needs it.

- **Anything else** goes in `compose.override.yaml` in the Mediaplane home. A port you
  publish there is held back too while the wizard is open, when the stack runs through
  `apply`. But `!reset` covers only `ports`: a `network_mode: host`, or a
  network shared with another service, publishes Jellyfin while its wizard is open. Keep
  those out of the override. The threat model lists what voids the guarantee:
  [T16](../../docs/security/threat-model.md#t16-someone-else-finishes-an-apps-first-run-setup).

## Known issues

- **A wizard finished by hand, before Slice 5.** `apply` can't sign in as the shared
  admin, so it can't make a key, and stops with
  `refused the shared admin's sign-in: its startup wizard was finished with another login`,
  with nothing after it. Jellyfin stays published, and until then, `apply` wires no app.
  When more follows the message, Jellyfin stays unpublished instead: the
  [wiring failed runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md) says what to do. For
  this one, set `admin.username`, and `admin.password` to a file of your own, to
  Jellyfin's admin login, and apply again: the other apps take that login too. A
  library of yours named Movies or Shows then becomes Mediaplane's: `plan` shows its
  folders changing, so rename it first to keep it.
  Or start Jellyfin afresh: stop Jellyfin first (`docker stop mediaplane-jellyfin-1`),
  then remove `appdata/jellyfin`, then run `apply`. That loses its database and settings,
  but not your media.
- **Its key deleted in Jellyfin's dashboard** (API Keys). `plan` warns that Jellyfin
  refuses Mediaplane's API key. Remove the `jellyfin` entry under `apps` from
  `state/secrets.json`, keeping the file valid JSON, and apply: Mediaplane signs in as the
  admin, makes a new key, and gives it to Sonarr and Radarr. Slice 10 does this for you.
  The [wiring failed runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md) has the details.
- **Its `appdata/` emptied by hand.** Jellyfin starts its wizard again. Stop Jellyfin
  first (`docker stop mediaplane-jellyfin-1`), then remove `appdata/jellyfin`, then run
  `apply`: it finds no `system.xml` saying the wizard is done, starts Jellyfin
  unpublished, and sets it up again, with a new key. A Jellyfin still running, or started
  again outside `apply`, with its appdata emptied, comes up published with its wizard
  open.
